name: Candesartan
summary: A potent ARB prodrug (candesartan cilexetil) with strong, dose-dependent blood-pressure lowering and heart-failure morbidity/mortality evidence from the CHARM program.
mechanism: Prodrug converted to candesartan during absorption; selectively blocks the AT1 angiotensin II receptor, reducing vasoconstriction and aldosterone release.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Minimal (O-deethylation to an inactive metabolite; minor CYP2C9)

dosing.adult: Hypertension: 16 mg once daily (range 8–32 mg); heart failure: start 4 mg once daily, double every 2 weeks to 32 mg once daily

safety.pregnancy: Contraindicated in second and third trimesters (fetotoxic)
warnings: Hyperkalemia, especially with ACE inhibitors or potassium-sparing agents
Rise in creatinine with renal impairment

indications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (CHARM program)
clinicalPearls: CHARM showed reduced cardiovascular death and heart-failure hospitalization in HFrEF — an indication many ARBs lack.
Once-daily dosing with a smooth 24-hour profile; among the more potent ARBs per milligram.
good: Hypertension and HFrEF where a once-daily ARB with hard-outcome evidence is wanted.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references (Goodman & Gilman, Katzung, Lexicomp-level standard facts). Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
